justification: Planned interim analysis permitted by protocol; no futility or harm stated; paediatric dose-ranging.
adjudication_note: keep dossier code: the trial stopped after a planned interim analysis with no futility or harm; the paediatric population is secondary (A1)

justification: Both stopped trials are in special populations: 2 mg nicotine gum versus placebo in pregnant smokers (DSMB stopped for lack of efficacy; final quit rates 13% vs 9.6%, no excess harm) and a 42 mg versus 21 mg patch dose comparison in schizophrenia (stopped, no difference between groups). Neither tests the labelled adult-smoker regimen, so neither shows nicotine ineffective for dependence.

Single-arm WHO-protocol efficacy study of standard-dose sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine in children 6-59 months with uncomplicated falciparum malaria, the labelled setting and regimen. Stopped after 29 of 139 planned children because of an early treatment failure; PCR-corrected response was only 46% with 92% dhfr triple mutants, while the drug was well tolerated. This is lack of efficacy through local resistance, not toxicity.
adjudication_note: source-verified code: the publication reports stopping for unexpectedly high treatment failure of standard sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine in its labelled setting (resistance)

justification: Registered with SP arms plus a chlorproguanil-dapsone (CD) arm, but the publication (Gesase 2009) reports only SP arms, stopped for unacceptable SP failure (82% total failure by day 28). CD could not be procured and was withdrawn from development, so dapsone was never given. The stop reflects failure of the comparator SP and drug unavailability, not dapsone efficacy or safety.

Single-arm mechanistic study of add-on metoprolol succinate (titrated to heart rate) in already controlled hypertensives on an ACE inhibitor or ARB, with cardiac MIBG sympathetic innervation as primary outcome. The PI closed it after an external publication linked beta-blockers as primary hypertension therapy with excess cardiac deaths; the posted results state no adverse reactions were observed in the study, and no outcome data were analysed.
adjudication_note: source-verified code: stopped by the investigator after an external publication; posted results report no adverse reactions

justification: Adjunct to gonadotropins for IVF in poor responders aged 35-45; outcome cycle cancellation.
adjudication_note: keep dossier code: co-treatment during IVF stimulation is a different treatment goal; poor-responder subgroup secondary

justification: Phase 2 trial of metformin versus placebo to prevent weight gain and metabolic syndrome caused by androgen deprivation in non-diabetic men with locally advanced prostate cancer on radiotherapy; the registered condition is prostate neoplasm, so the metabolic-syndrome link is indirect. Stopped after an interim analysis found no significant weight difference (no benefit at 1 year in the paper). Different population and prevention goal, not metabolic syndrome as usually treated.

Sponsor trial in Chinese adults of olanzapine plus fluoxetine versus placebo plus fluoxetine for treatment-resistant depression (failure of two antidepressants), matching the labelled combination, population definition and dose range. Stopped at interim for lack of efficacy: MADRS difference -1.62 (95% CI -5.04 to 1.80) with a large control-arm response. The only departure from the label is the regional population.

Single-arm phase II of a new triplet (gemcitabine, capecitabine, bevacizumab for six cycles, then bevacizumab to one year) as adjuvant consolidation after neoadjuvant chemotherapy in residual breast cancer; gemcitabine's labelled use is with paclitaxel in metastatic disease. Stopped after 18 enrolments because the DSMB judged the regimen more toxic than expected (6 of 17 left for toxicity) and accrual was slow; harm belongs to the triplet.

Randomised phase III in untreated advanced gastric cancer comparing experimental fractionated docetaxel-oxaliplatin-capecitabine (Low-TOX) with the standard EOX regimen, whose epirubicin arm is the control. The interim futility analysis found no benefit of Low-TOX (median PFS 6.3 vs 6.3 months); EOX performed as expected and remains a potential standard. The stop reflects failure of the experimental regimen, not of epirubicin.

Fluoxetine 20 mg/day was given in both arms; the randomised variable was the 5-HT1A antagonist DU-125530 versus placebo. The interim analysis showed no difference between arms, and the publication reports that the add-on neither accelerated nor augmented fluoxetine's effect. The failure belongs to the add-on, not to fluoxetine in major depression.

Single-arm neoadjuvant trial of weekly paclitaxel, then weekly doxorubicin plus daily oral cyclophosphamide 100 mg, without G-CSF: a metronomic multi-drug variant, not a standard regimen. The publication says closure followed pneumonitis in the sister HER2-positive cohort given trastuzumab, plus SWOG 0012 results; TAME itself had no febrile neutropenia. Harm specific to cyclophosphamide is not shown.

Adjuvant MVAC versus observation was tested only in p53-altered, organ-confined pT1-T2 N0 patients after cystectomy, not an established setting for methotrexate-containing regimens (neoadjuvant in muscle-invasive disease and advanced disease are). The DSMB halted accrual after a futility analysis; the authors state that refusals, low event rates and undelivered MVAC severely compromised power (recurrence HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.29-2.08).

Methotrexate (7.5 to 20 mg/week) was given in every arm, with placebo plus methotrexate as control; the randomised agent was ocrelizumab. The sponsor ended the ocrelizumab programme on benefit-risk grounds, mainly serious infections at 500 mg, while both doses reduced radiographic progression versus methotrexate alone. Nothing concerns methotrexate's own efficacy or safety.

Withdrawn before any participant was enrolled (0 of 50 planned); the stated reason, lack of data, reports no efficacy or safety finding. The design compared high-dose fluticasone with medium-dose fluticasone followed by salmeterol/fluticasone, with blood neutrophil priming as a mechanistic primary outcome, so no result bears on fluticasone in asthma.

The sponsor terminated the trial after HPS2-THRIVE, a separate trial in vascular disease, showed no benefit and more serious adverse events with niacin/laropiprant. This trial enrolled low-to-moderate-risk South and Southeast Asians with dyslipidaemia, not coronary disease, and posted no efficacy analysis (70 completers; one serious adverse event on active drug).

The DSMB stopped the trial for a pre-specified imbalance in deaths, but deaths were fewer with galantamine (33 vs 56 with placebo; HR 0.58, p=0.011), and the MMSE primary outcome also favoured galantamine (p<0.001). The stop followed a favourable result in labelled mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease; the 'safety' classification is a mislabel.

Single-arm trial of transdermal estradiol 0.4 mg/day in men with metastatic prostate cancer that progressed after hormone therapy and docetaxel; the label covers oral estradiol for advanced androgen-dependent disease, for palliation only. PSA response was 8.7% and the study was stopped as ineffective, so it tested a later, castration-resistant stage and a different formulation.

Oral estradiol 10 mg three times daily, the labelled palliative breast-cancer dose, was tested only in receptor-negative, HER2-negative (triple-negative) metastatic disease. One partial response in 17 patients and median progression-free survival of 1.9 months closed the trial after stage 1. High-dose estrogen is traditionally used in hormone-receptor-positive disease, so this is a narrow subtype outside the established population.

The registry reason is ethical issues of continuing a control group without treatment, which is no efficacy or safety finding about the drug; the 2-year result favoured the intensive arm (-9.7% vs -0.4% in completers). Diethylpropion was one optional drug, beside sibutramine or orlistat, in a multicomponent programme of liquid diet, meal replacement and group therapy lasting years, unlike the labelled short-term monotherapy.

Phase 4 GSK study withdrawn before any participant was enrolled (actual enrolment 0); 'lack of data' reports no efficacy or safety finding, so the Open Targets 'Negative' category is a mapping error. Design was a mechanistic comparison of high-dose fluticasone with fluticasone/salmeterol in allergic asthma, using neutrophil priming as the endpoint.

Phase III of first-line maintenance in ER-positive HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer: exemestane plus bevacizumab replaced the taxane, versus continued paclitaxel plus bevacizumab. Enrolment was stopped after a futility interim analysis (7% chance of a significant PFS gain; HR 1.0). This tests a new maintenance strategy, not exemestane in its labelled adjuvant or post-tamoxifen settings.
adjudication_note: source-verified code: first-line maintenance differs from the labelled adjuvant and post-tamoxifen settings; comparison with continued chemotherapy secondary (C)

justification: Phase III of three cycles of adjuvant MVAC versus observation after cystectomy in node-negative, organ-confined (pT1-T2 N0) bladder cancer selected for p53 alteration. This is outside doxorubicin's labelled metastatic bladder indication. Accrual was halted after a futility review; the paper found no recurrence benefit (HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.29-2.08) in a trial whose power was severely compromised.

Both trials place doxorubicin in new combinations, not standard dosing: a single-arm metronomic paclitaxel, doxorubicin and oral cyclophosphamide regimen, closed partly for pneumonitis in its HER2-positive sister cohort and for external SWOG 0012 data, and a phase Ib of liposomal doxorubicin plus lapatinib, where only dose level 3 was dropped and the combination was judged feasible.

Phase 1/2 of the IGF-1R/insulin receptor inhibitor KW-2450 added to lapatinib plus letrozole, a labelled combination in postmenopausal HR-positive HER2-positive advanced disease. Dose-limiting rash and hyperglycemia arose in the KW-2450 combination; the paper reports a recommended phase 2 dose but no phase 2 because of anticipated enrolment difficulty and the end of KW-2450 development. Letrozole was a fixed partner.

Randomized placebo-controlled trial of cinacalcet in children aged 6 to 17 on dialysis with secondary hyperparathyroidism; the established indication is adults on dialysis. Dosing was stopped and the study closed after a fatality in a severely hypocalcemic cinacalcet-treated child whose death was multifactorial, with a drug contribution not excluded. The primary efficacy endpoint was met (55% vs 19%).

Pragmatic phase 4 trial of intensive medical management for class III obesity (low-calorie diet, group counselling and a physician-chosen drug: orlistat, sibutramine or diethylpropion) versus website-based usual care. It stopped because an untreated control group was judged unethical while the sponsor pursued a coverage policy, not for an efficacy or safety finding; the intensive arm lost more weight (completers -9.7% vs -0.4%).

Both stopped trials add capecitabine to new combinations: a single-arm adjuvant gemcitabine, capecitabine and bevacizumab regimen after neoadjuvant therapy (monitoring board found excess toxicity; 6 of 17 left for toxicity) and the phase III TABEA trial adding capecitabine to first-line taxane plus bevacizumab (no benefit, more grade 3-4 events). Neither is the labelled single-agent or docetaxel-doublet use.

Pragmatic phase 4 trial of intensive medical management for class III obesity (low-calorie diet, group counselling and a physician-chosen drug: sibutramine, orlistat or diethylpropion) versus website-based usual care. It stopped because an untreated control group was judged unethical while the sponsor pursued a coverage policy, not for an efficacy or safety finding about sibutramine; the intensive arm lost more weight (completers -9.7% vs -0.4%).

Postmarketing safety trial of pioglitazone versus glyburide in type 2 diabetes with NYHA class II or early III heart failure and ejection fraction below 40%, a comorbid group for which the Actos label carries a boxed warning. The monitoring board stopped it for more heart-failure hospitalizations on pioglitazone (composite 13% vs 8%). This confirms a labelled class risk, not failure of glycaemic control.

Randomised escitalopram 10 mg versus placebo for major depression in 24 patients with advanced lung or gastrointestinal cancer (220 planned). The DSMB stopped it because worsening depression scores and deaths were more frequent on placebo, so the harm came from the comparator, not escitalopram. Cancer is a comorbidity subgroup of an established use.

Single-arm feasibility study of weekly paclitaxel, then weekly doxorubicin plus daily oral cyclophosphamide (metronomic, no routine G-CSF), in locally advanced HER2-negative breast cancer. The paper attributes closure to severe pneumonitis in the parallel paclitaxel-trastuzumab cohort and to SWOG 0012 data, not to a paclitaxel-specific finding. A new multi-drug regimen, not established paclitaxel use.

Open-label two-year safety study of flexible-dose aripiprazole in 524 children and adolescents (schizophrenia or bipolar I). Posted text says the sponsor ended it because the EMA paediatric investigational plan requirement (two years of safety data in at least 100 participants) was met in April 2014. No efficacy or safety finding triggered the stop; adolescent schizophrenia is a labelled use.

Single-arm phase II of docetaxel plus celecoxib in chemotherapy-naive androgen-independent prostate cancer, run November 2004 to April 2005 with 6 patients. The stated reason is celecoxib safety issues, matching the NIH suspension of celecoxib for cardiovascular risk on 17 December 2004. No docetaxel efficacy or safety finding exists; docetaxel was the fixed partner of the agent causing concern.

Randomised phase III (LEGA) of fractionated low-dose docetaxel plus oxaliplatin and capecitabine versus EOX in first-line advanced gastric cancer, stopped at a planned futility analysis because superiority over EOX was not shown. Median progression-free survival was identical (6.3 months), so the docetaxel triplet was as active as the standard; the question was comparative.

Single-arm phase II (UNICANCER/GERICO) of biweekly docetaxel as first-line chemotherapy in women aged 70 or older with metastatic breast cancer, with autonomy as primary outcome, stopped for unspecified toxicity. A special population on a non-standard schedule; toxicity details are unavailable, so it does not show failure of docetaxel in its established every-3-week use.

Both trials are early-phase combinations containing lapatinib: KW-2450 plus lapatinib and letrozole, and lapatinib plus liposomal doxorubicin. Papers show a recommended dose was found in each; the KW-2450 programme ended for enrolment difficulty and sponsor decision, and the second stopped escalation after slow accrual and grade 3 events. Neither tests lapatinib in an established regimen.

Both trials test everolimus preoperatively in early breast cancer, whereas its label covers advanced HR-positive disease with exemestane. NCT02236572 (aromatase inhibitor plus everolimus) stopped when only 4 of 15 reached PEPI 0 (5 needed); NCT00674414 (trastuzumab plus everolimus, HER2-positive) closed for slow accrual and showed no efficacy gain. Neither tests the established setting.

Single-arm phase II of degarelix 240/80 mg in men with non-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer and PSA progression on total androgen blockade; 5 enrolled and the investigator ended the study as negative. The label evidence base is men starting androgen deprivation (baseline testosterone about 400 ng/dL), so this refractory-stage test does not contradict the indication.

INFORMS tested fingolimod 0.5 mg versus placebo in primary progressive multiple sclerosis; the core trial missed its primary endpoint (hazard ratio 0.95 for confirmed disability progression) and the open-label extension was terminated. The label covers relapsing forms, so this is a different subtype and does not contradict the indication.

PARADIGM-HF (LCZ696 = sacubitril/valsartan vs enalapril, 8,442 HFrEF patients) was stopped early because the prespecified boundary for overwhelming benefit was crossed (primary composite 21.8% vs 26.5%, HR 0.80). A stop for benefit is no efficacy or safety failure; valsartan is the fixed partner of the new agent sacubitril, and the comparator was enalapril.

Pediatric (6-16 years) placebo-controlled dose-response study of ramipril, stopped after a planned interim analysis 'as permitted by protocol'; no futility or safety reason is given. Posted results show a larger systolic fall with high-dose ramipril than placebo (-11.3 vs -8.1 mmHg, p=0.044) and no safety signal. The US label lists hypertension but states that pediatric safety and effectiveness are not established.

Both stopped trials enrolled special populations: smokers with schizophrenia (42 mg vs 21 mg patch, stopped when interim analysis showed no difference between doses) and pregnant smokers (2 mg gum vs placebo; the DSMB stopped enrolment for lack of efficacy, quit rates 13% vs 9.6%). Neither tested the labelled adult cessation regimen against placebo; the label caps the patch at one 21 mg patch/day and restricts use in pregnancy.

Single-arm WHO-style efficacy study of single-dose sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine in children aged 6-59 months with uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Gabon, matching the Fansidar label setting and regimen. Investigators stopped after 29 children because of early treatment failure; the paper reports 54% PCR-corrected failure and 92% dhfr triple mutants, with SP well tolerated. This is loss of efficacy to resistance, not toxicity.

Single-arm mechanistic study (I-123 MIBG cardiac sympathetic innervation) adding metoprolol succinate to an ACE inhibitor or ARB in controlled hypertension. The PI closed it after a publication reported excess cardiac mortality with beta-blockers as primary hypertension therapy; the posted results state that no adverse reactions were seen. 24 enrolled, 4 completed, no analysable outcome data. External evidence, not a trial finding, caused the stop.

Open-label comparison of lidocaine 5% patch with celecoxib 200 mg in knee osteoarthritis was terminated by the sponsor for class safety concerns about COX-2 inhibitors (the comparator), not for any lidocaine finding. The publication (143 randomised) found no significant differences in WOMAC pain or tolerability (treatment-related events 11.6% vs 10.8%). Knee osteoarthritis is also off-label for the Lidoderm patch.

Phase II single-agent mitomycin-C in previously untreated advanced pancreatic adenocarcinoma with a BRCA2 mutation was withdrawn with zero enrolment because every consented patient tested negative for BRCA2. No patient was treated, so there is no efficacy or safety finding. The design (BRCA2-selected, single-agent, first-line) also differs from the label, which does not recommend single-agent primary therapy.

Single-arm pilot of 4 weeks of preoperative gefitinib in resectable stage I-IIIA NSCLC without EGFR selection, not the labelled use (first-line metastatic EGFR-mutant NSCLC). It closed when the prespecified low-response stopping rule was met (22 of 23 treated had stable disease, 1 progression), so the failure is lack of activity in the neoadjuvant setting, not in the established indication.

Phase 3 trial of olanzapine added to fluoxetine versus placebo plus fluoxetine in Chinese adults with treatment-resistant depression as defined in the olanzapine/fluoxetine label (two failed antidepressants in the current episode). Stopped at interim assessment for lack of efficacy; 8-week MADRS change -15.9 vs -14.3 (difference -1.6, 95% CI -5.0 to 1.8). Population and regimen class match the label; the sample was Chinese only.

The same trial of olanzapine plus fluoxetine in Chinese adults with treatment-resistant depression (stopped for lack of efficacy) is attached to an 'anxiety disorder' concept that merges 12 MONDO terms, including depressive disorder and mood disorder. No anxiety disorder was studied and no olanzapine label covers one, so the link is a mapping artefact; whether it contradicts the recorded indication depends on which member carries it.
adjudication_note: source-verified code: the depression trial reaches a lumped anxiety-disorder concept; the sources do not show which member carries the recorded indication

justification: TRUST-1 (45 patients, India) was suspended on DSMB advice; published efficacy was positive (placebo-corrected 6-minute walk +83 m, p=0.008). Safety reviewers cited delayed rescue therapy for outpatient IV infusion because of limited healthcare infrastructure: a setting and route problem, not drug failure, although no drug-attributable harm is documented either.

Single-arm phase II adding the investigational agent OSI-906 to standard sorafenib 400 mg twice daily in advanced HCC. Stopped after 3 patients because of a safety signal for OSI-906 in a parallel HCC study; this trial reported no serious adverse events and no efficacy data. Sorafenib was the fixed partner, not the agent under test.

Both stopped trials added an investigational agent to full-dose sorafenib in advanced HCC. NCT00971126 (plus escalating thalidomide) was closed by the DSMB after dose-limiting toxicity in two patients at the first dose level; NCT01334710 (plus OSI-906) stopped on an external safety signal with no serious adverse events. Neither tested sorafenib alone.

Takeda's Japanese phase 3 compared lansoprazole 15 mg daily with gefarnate for preventing ulcer recurrence in patients on long-term low-dose aspirin. An efficacy committee stopped it at interim analysis because lansoprazole was superior (ulcers 6/226 vs 53/234, HR 0.099). This is a stop for benefit; the 'Negative' category appears to misread 'superior to gefarnate'.

Fluoxetine 20 mg/day was given in both arms; the trial tested whether adding the 5-HT1A antagonist DU-125530 speeds or augments response. The interim analysis at 50 of 100 planned patients showed no group difference, so the add-on failed. Both arms improved significantly over time, so fluoxetine's efficacy is not in question.
Boosted protease-inhibitor strategy trials: immediate versus deferred therapy, monotherapy simplification, PI pairing, post-exposure prophylaxis.
adjudication_note: keep dossier code: early infection, post-exposure prophylaxis and simplification strategies; ritonavir as booster in new combinations secondary (B2)

justification: Erlotinib was combined with a new partner or modality in all four trials: digoxin (1 response in 24), bortezomib (9% vs 16% response for erlotinib alone), whole-brain radiotherapy in unselected brain metastases (no benefit) and LY2584702 (dose-limiting toxicity). None stopped because erlotinib alone failed in its established second-line setting.
adjudication_note: source-verified code: the publication shows that the erlotinib-plus-bortezomib arm, not erlotinib alone, was stopped for insufficient activity

justification: Oral cyclophosphamide with dexamethasone was the fixed partner of the investigational proteasome inhibitor oprozomib in one 3-patient cohort. Amgen halted dose escalation because the oprozomib formulation's safety and pharmacokinetics needed optimisation. The cyclophosphamide cohort had no dose-limiting toxicity and no adverse-event discontinuations; the stop concerned oprozomib.

Propranolol was the experimental arm against prednisolone in infants aged 2 weeks to 6 months with symptomatic proliferating haemangioma. The trial stopped because of serious adverse events (growth failure, adrenal crisis) on prednisolone: 11 serious events versus 1 with propranolol, with similar lesion shrinkage. The harm came from the comparator.

GSK's phase 4 mechanistic study (high-dose fluticasone propionate versus fluticasone then salmeterol/fluticasone, neutrophil-priming biomarker endpoint) was withdrawn before enrolling anyone; the registry reason is 'lack of data'. With zero participants there is no efficacy or safety finding, so the Negative classification rests only on the wording of the reason.

AIM-HIGH: extended-release niacin added to simvastatin in established vascular disease; stopped for lack of efficacy. Statin background is current practice, so this is a failure in the setting where niacin would be used.
adjudication_note: keep dossier code: AIM-HIGH tested niacin in its population with statin background, the setting of current use; FDA withdrew the statin co-administration indications citing it

justification: Single-arm trial of LAMPP (L-asparaginase, methotrexate, pegylated liposomal doxorubicin, prednisone) in relapsed or refractory peripheral and advanced cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, stopped for 'toxicity'. Prednisone is one of four agents in a new combination, and no results or publication name the toxicity or the agent, so the stop does not bear on prednisone's established use in lymphoma regimens.

EVOLVE compared tobramycin inhalation powder with placebo in cystic fibrosis with P. aeruginosa (age 6-21, FEV1 25-80% predicted) and was stopped on the data monitoring committee's recommendation after a planned interim analysis showed significant benefit (FEV1 +13.3 points, P=0.0016). The 'Negative' tag misreads a favourable stop; only the dry-powder formulation was new, within the labelled population.

Single-arm phase II of oral estradiol 10 mg three times daily, the labelled palliative breast cancer dose, in metastatic triple-negative (ER-alpha/PgR-negative) disease, tested on an ER-beta hypothesis. The Simon two-stage design closed after stage 1 (1/17 responses, 5.9%). Estrogen therapy is traditionally used in hormone-receptor-positive disease, so a receptor-negative subtype failed, not the established use.

LOSS compared an intensive medical programme (liquid diet, group counselling, and sibutramine, orlistat or diethylpropion chosen by the physician) with website-only usual care in BMI 40-60. The stated reason was the ethics of leaving the control group untreated, and the programme clearly won (completers -9.7% vs -0.4% weight, P<0.001), so no efficacy or safety finding against diethylpropion exists.

TARDIS tested 30 days of triple antiplatelet therapy (aspirin, clopidogrel, dipyridamole) against guideline therapy (clopidogrel alone, or aspirin plus dipyridamole) within 48 hours of stroke or TIA. The DMC stopped it for excess major bleeding and futility (recurrence cOR 0.90; bleeding cOR 2.54). The harm came from intensification, and aspirin stayed in part of the guideline comparator.
Rituximab plus ESHAP in relapsed or refractory aggressive lymphoma; low response rate.
adjudication_note: keep dossier code: the tested regimen was a new combination (rituximab added to ESHAP); methylprednisolone is a fixed partner of the backbone

justification: Takeda's postmarketing study compared pioglitazone with glyburide for up to 24 weeks in type 2 diabetes with NYHA class II-III systolic heart failure (LVEF <40%); the DSMB stopped it for more heart-failure events on pioglitazone (primary endpoint 13% vs 8%). Symptomatic heart failure lies outside pioglitazone's recommended population, so the harm does not contradict its glycaemic-control indication.

Placebo-controlled trial of escitalopram 10 mg daily for major depression in advanced lung or gastrointestinal cancer; 24 of 220 planned patients were randomised. The DSMB stopped it because the placebo arm had more adverse events (two cancer deaths in placebo-first arms, none in the escitalopram-first arm), so harm came from the comparator, not from escitalopram.

Single-arm phase II adding vorinostat to the FND backbone (fludarabine, mitoxantrone, dexamethasone) in relapsed or refractory mantle cell lymphoma. The registry gives an efficacy futility stop (fewer than 7 responses in 19), but the published interim analysis reports a 77.8% response rate with heavy toxicity, so the real stop reason is unclear. Dexamethasone is a fixed partner; vorinostat is the new agent.

Single-arm pilot of weekly low-dose (metronomic) docetaxel plus sorafenib, first-line, in PS-2 non-squamous NSCLC, not the established single-agent second-line or platinum-doublet use. Stopped after 5 patients (target 43) when funding was withdrawn and efficacy looked unpromising (0 objective responses, 4/5 progression-free at 2 months, 4/5 serious adverse events). The novel combination, not docetaxel itself, was tested.

Phase II of biweekly docetaxel (days 1 and 15 of 28-day cycles) as first-line therapy in women aged 70 or over with metastatic breast cancer, with preserved autonomy (IADL) as primary endpoint. This is a special elderly population and a non-label schedule, not docetaxel's established 3-weekly regimen. Stopped for 'toxicity issues'; no data or full publication found.

Single-arm open-label lisdexamfetamine study in children and adolescents (8-17 years) with ADHD, obesity and glucose intolerance, assessing glucose metabolism. Of 14 screened, 12 failed screening (mostly lab criteria for glucose intolerance) and only 2 were treated; no outcome data were analysed. Stopped for recruitment and feasibility, not for efficacy or safety.

Two phase I dose-finding combinations that include lapatinib as a co-escalated partner: KW-2450 plus lapatinib and letrozole, and lapatinib plus pegylated liposomal doxorubicin. The KW-2450 triplet reached a recommended phase 2 dose, but phase 2 was not pursued (anticipated enrolment difficulty; KW-2450 development ended). In the liposomal doxorubicin study, dose level 3 was dropped for grade 3 toxicity and level 2 was judged feasible. Neither shows lapatinib failure.

Both trials put everolimus into early-stage breast cancer rather than the approved advanced HR-positive, HER2-negative, post-aromatase-inhibitor use: a preoperative HER2-positive trastuzumab add-on (stopped for accrual, no efficacy gain) and a neoadjuvant aromatase-inhibitor combination (stopped after 4/15 evaluable patients reached PEPI 0, below the 5/15 needed to continue).

Both trials moved trabectedin into first-line advanced soft tissue sarcoma against doxorubicin (one adding it to doxorubicin), whereas the label use is after an anthracycline-containing regimen. TRUSTS (n=133) ended for lack of superiority (median PFS 2.8 or 3.1 vs 5.5 months); GEIS-20 (n=115) stopped for futility (5.7 vs 5.5 months) with more toxicity. Neither tested the labelled post-anthracycline setting.
adjudication_note: source-verified code: first-line use against doxorubicin, whereas the label is after an anthracycline; comparison secondary (C)

justification: TRIGGER-PCI: prasugrel versus clopidogrel after elective PCI; stopped for a low event rate.
adjudication_note: keep dossier code: stopped for futility because of a very low event rate, which is no efficacy finding; stable coronary disease population secondary (A2)

justification: CHAMPION PCI tested the labelled cangrelor bolus-plus-infusion as PCI adjunct (ACS and stable angina) against 600 mg clopidogrel given just before PCI. It was stopped for futility at the 70% interim analysis: death, MI or revascularisation at 48 hours 7.5% vs 7.1% (OR 1.05), with no safety issues reported by the sponsor. Approval later rested on CHAMPION PHOENIX, whose design differed.

Single-arm phase II of degarelix at the labelled 240/80 mg monthly regimen in non-metastatic hormone-refractory prostate cancer, with PSA rising despite castrate testosterone on LHRH agonist plus anti-androgen. The label rests on initial androgen deprivation in advanced disease (baseline testosterone about 400 ng/dL), not this castration-resistant switch. Five patients enrolled; the investigator stopped it as a 'negative study'. No data or publication.

Planned phase 1/2 PrEP study of long-acting injectable rilpivirine (TMC278LA 600 mg intramuscular monthly) in HIV-negative healthy volunteers, a prevention use with a depot formulation, unlike the labelled oral treatment of HIV-1 infection. Closed with zero participants enrolled citing 'additional safety information' of unspecified origin, so the trial produced no safety or efficacy data.
